Test each trait within each taxonomic/biogeographic group for normality.

# Select relevant variables and group by taxonomic group separating montanus into NORTH and SOUTH groups and japonicus into CONTINENTAL and OCEANIC groups and create datasets with the original data and log transformed data. 
ZosteropsMorph_groups <- ZosteropsMorph %>%
  select(Group, BillCulmen, BillNareTip, BillDepth, BillWidth, Tarsus, Wing, Tail) %>%
  group_by(Group)

# Function to perform Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for each variable within each group
perform_ks_test <- function(group_data, variable) {
  # Create a list to store results
  results <- list()
  
  # Get unique groups
  unique_groups <- unique(group_data$Group)
  
  # Iterate over each unique group
  for (i in 1:length(unique_groups)) {
    # Filter data for the specific group
    group_name <- unique_groups[i]
    group_values <- group_data %>% filter(Group == group_name) %>% pull(variable)
    
    # Perform KS test with the first group's data as reference
    if (i == 1) {
      reference_values <- group_values
    } else {
      ks_test_result <- ks.test(group_values, reference_values)
      results[[group_name]] <- ks_test_result
    }
  }
  return(results)
}

# Define a function to create boxplots for each trait
create_boxplot <- function(data, trait) {
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = "Group", y = trait)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + # Boxplot without outliers
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, aes(color = Group), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + # Add jitter for individual points
    scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) + # Define colors for groups
    theme_minimal() + # Minimal theme for better aesthetics
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) # Adjust labels on X axis
}

Estimate Fst and Nei’s distance
Generate the Fst and Nei’s distance estimates from the Zosterops genlight object (ZosteropsGEN).

ZosteropsFST <- stamppFst(ZosteropsGEN, nboots = 100, percent = 95, nclusters = 4)
ZosteropsFSTmatrix <- ZosteropsFST$Fsts
ZosteropsFSTmatrix[upper.tri(ZosteropsFSTmatrix)] <- t(ZosteropsFSTmatrix)[upper.tri(ZosteropsFSTmatrix)]
ZosteropsFSTheat <- reshape::melt(ZosteropsFSTmatrix)

Combined Fst and Nei’s distance
Combined Fst and Nei’s distance figure with combined groupings. These data are more precise given the groupings have larger sample sizes and are used for the main figure of the text while the more subdivided scheme appears in the appendix with cautions regarding small sample size for some groups.

Combined group assignments
Populations from the ZosteropsPOPS_distance.txt assignment file were merged into the following broader groups, and FST and Nei’s distance were re-estimated for these groups rather than averaged from the subdivided estimates. Sample sizes (number of individuals in the filtered SNP dataset) are given in parentheses.

Zosterops japonicus

japonicus continental (27) The Korean Peninsula and the main islands and Ryukyu archipelago of Japan, combining japonicusKOREA (8), japonicusJAPAN (4), japonicusRYUKYUn (2), japonicusRYUKYUc (9), and japonicusRYUKYUs (4).
japonicus Izu (6) Z. japonicus stejnegeri from the Izu Islands (japonicusIZU).
japonicus Ogasawara (7) Z. japonicus alani from the Ogasawara and Volcano Islands (japonicusOGASAWARA).

Zosterops meyeni

meyeni (12) Lanyu and the Batan Islands, combining meyeniBATAN (8) and meyeniLANYU (4).

Zosterops montanus

montanus N Philippines (6) Luzon and Mindoro (montanusNORTH).
montanus S Philippines (15) The Visayas and Mindanao, combining montanusVISAYAS (9) and montanusMINDANAO (6). As in the subdivided analysis, this group includes the sample from Camiguin South (Zni14341) originally assigned to Z. nigrorum catarmanensis.

Other taxa

everetti (3) Z. everetti (unchanged).
nigrorum (4) Z. nigrorum, excluding the Camiguin South sample (unchanged).
simplex (21) Z. simplex from Taiwan and mainland Asia (simplexASIA).


The following groups were excluded from the combined analysis: the introduced populations in Hawaii (japonicusHAWAII) and North America (simplexNA), groups with very small samples (montanusPALAWAN, 2; montanusINDONESIA, 3), and the outgroup taxa erythropleurus and palpebrosus.

# ---- Combine populations into larger groups ----
combine <- c(
  japonicusJAPAN   = "japonicus continental", japonicusKOREA   = "japonicus continental",
  japonicusRYUKYUn = "japonicus continental", japonicusRYUKYUc = "japonicus continental",
  japonicusRYUKYUs = "japonicus continental",
  japonicusIZU = "japonicus Izu", japonicusOGASAWARA = "japonicus Ogasawara",
  meyeniBATAN = "meyeni", meyeniLANYU = "meyeni",
  montanusNORTH = "montanus N Philippines",
  montanusVISAYAS = "montanus S Philippines", montanusMINDANAO = "montanus S Philippines",
  simplexASIA = "simplex", everetti = "everetti", nigrorum = "nigrorum")
# Groups not listed (japonicusHAWAII, montanusPALAWAN, montanusINDONESIA, simplexNA,
# erythropleurus, palpebrosus) are excluded

# Axis order matches the subdivided (Appendix) heatmap
ord <- c("japonicus continental", "japonicus Izu", "japonicus Ogasawara", "meyeni",
         "montanus N Philippines", "montanus S Philippines", "simplex",
         "everetti", "nigrorum")

newpop  <- combine[as.character(pop(ZosteropsGEN))]
GENcomb <- ZosteropsGEN[!is.na(newpop)]
pop(GENcomb) <- factor(newpop[!is.na(newpop)], levels = ord)
print(table(pop(GENcomb)))               # check group sizes


 japonicus continental          japonicus Izu    japonicus Ogasawara 
                    27                      6                      7 
                meyeni montanus N Philippines montanus S Philippines 
                    12                      6                     15 
               simplex               everetti               nigrorum 
                    21                      3                      4 

# ---- Re-estimate Fst and Nei's D for the combined groups ----
FSTcomb <- stamppFst(GENcomb, nboots = 100, percent = 95, nclusters = 4)
fst <- as.matrix(FSTcomb$Fsts)
fst[upper.tri(fst)] <- t(fst)[upper.tri(fst)]
nei <- as.matrix(stamppNeisD(GENcomb, pop = TRUE))
dimnames(nei) <- list(rownames(nei), rownames(nei))
stopifnot(setequal(ord, rownames(fst)), setequal(ord, rownames(nei)))

fst <- fst[ord, ord]; nei <- nei[ord, ord]
n   <- as.vector(table(pop(GENcomb))[ord])
lab <- paste0(ord, " (", n, ")")          # axis labels with sample sizes

# ---- Build cells: i = row (bottom -> top), j = column (left -> right) ----
idx <- expand.grid(i = seq_along(ord), j = seq_along(ord))
cells <- data.frame(X = factor(lab[idx$j], levels = lab),
                    Y = factor(lab[idx$i], levels = lab),
                    i = idx$i, j = idx$j,
                    FST = fst[cbind(idx$i, idx$j)],
                    NEI = nei[cbind(idx$i, idx$j)])

# ---- Plot: Fst above the diagonal (upper left), Nei's D below (lower right) ----
ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = subset(cells, i > j), aes(X, Y, fill = FST), colour = "white") +
  geom_text(data = subset(cells, i > j), aes(X, Y, label = sprintf("%.2f", FST)), size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red", limits = c(0, NA),
                      name = expression(F[ST])) +
  new_scale_fill() +
  geom_tile(data = subset(cells, i < j), aes(X, Y, fill = NEI), colour = "white") +
  geom_text(data = subset(cells, i < j), aes(X, Y, label = sprintf("%.3f", NEI)), size = 3.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red", limits = c(0, NA),
                      name = "Nei's D") +
  geom_tile(data = subset(cells, i == j), aes(X, Y), fill = "grey55", colour = "white") +
  coord_equal() +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = lab) +        # pin both axes to the same order
  scale_y_discrete(limits = lab) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        panel.grid = element_blank())











Sensitivity of FST and Nei’s distance to sample size
Sample sizes differ widely among the combined groups (3–27 individuals). Nei’s D (Nei 1972), as computed in StAMPP, has no small-sample correction and is biased upward when few individuals are sampled, while Weir & Cockerham’s FST corrects for sample size but becomes more variable. To check whether the patterns in the combined heatmap depend on sample size, we repeatedly subsampled every combined group to the same number of individuals (n = 4 and n = 3; 100 replicates each) and recalculated pairwise FST and Nei’s D. At n = 4, Z. everetti (n = 3) is omitted. At n = 3, all groups are compared at equal sample size.

set.seed(20261008)
nrep  <- 100
sizes <- c(4, 3)
grp_all <- as.character(pop(GENcomb))
lev     <- levels(pop(GENcomb))

# Helper: one row per pair from a StAMPP Fst matrix (lower triangle) and a Nei's D matrix
pair_values <- function(f, d, groups) {
  pr <- t(combn(groups, 2))
  data.frame(A = pr[, 1], B = pr[, 2],
             Fst = mapply(function(a, b) ifelse(is.na(f[a, b]), f[b, a], f[a, b]), pr[, 1], pr[, 2]),
             Nei = d[cbind(pr[, 1], pr[, 2])],
             row.names = NULL)
}

# Full-sample values
f_full <- as.matrix(stamppFst(GENcomb, nboots = 0, nclusters = 1))
d_full <- as.matrix(stamppNeisD(GENcomb, pop = TRUE)); dimnames(d_full) <- list(rownames(d_full), rownames(d_full))
full <- pair_values(f_full, d_full, lev)

# Rarefied values
rare <- do.call(rbind, lapply(sizes, function(k) {
  keep <- intersect(lev, names(which(table(grp_all) >= k)))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrep), function(r) {
    idx <- unlist(lapply(keep, function(g) sample(which(grp_all == g), k)))
    sub <- GENcomb[idx]
    pop(sub) <- factor(as.character(pop(sub)), levels = keep)
    f <- as.matrix(stamppFst(sub, nboots = 0, nclusters = 1))
    d <- as.matrix(stamppNeisD(sub, pop = TRUE)); dimnames(d) <- list(rownames(d), rownames(d))
    cbind(n = k, rep = r, pair_values(f, d, keep))
  }))
}))

# Summarize: mean and 95% interval across replicates
summ <- aggregate(cbind(Fst, Nei) ~ n + A + B, data = rare,
                  FUN = function(x) c(mean = mean(x), lo = unname(quantile(x, 0.025)), hi = unname(quantile(x, 0.975))))
summ <- do.call(data.frame, summ)
wide <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("A", "B"), all.x = TRUE),
               list(setNames(full, c("A", "B", "Fst_full", "Nei_full")),
                    setNames(subset(summ, n == 4)[, -1], c("A", "B", paste0(c("Fst_", "Fst_", "Fst_", "Nei_", "Nei_", "Nei_"), c("n4", "n4_lo", "n4_hi", "n4", "n4_lo", "n4_hi")))),
                    setNames(subset(summ, n == 3)[, -1], c("A", "B", paste0(c("Fst_", "Fst_", "Fst_", "Nei_", "Nei_", "Nei_"), c("n3", "n3_lo", "n3_hi", "n3", "n3_lo", "n3_hi"))))))
wide <- wide[order(match(wide$A, lev), match(wide$B, lev)), ]
write.csv(wide, "Fst_NeisD_rarefaction.csv", row.names = FALSE)

knitr::kable(transform(wide[, c("A", "B", "Fst_full", "Fst_n4", "Fst_n3", "Nei_full", "Nei_n4", "Nei_n3")],
                       Fst_full = round(Fst_full, 3), Fst_n4 = round(Fst_n4, 3), Fst_n3 = round(Fst_n3, 3),
                       Nei_full = round(Nei_full, 4), Nei_n4 = round(Nei_n4, 4), Nei_n3 = round(Nei_n3, 4)),

Define color values for box plots to match prior color schemes.

species_colors <- c("#004949", "#DB6D00", "#D82632", "#FED439", "#FA9C88", "#924900", "#8DB6CD", "#CDAA7D", "#008600")

Create box-and-whisker plots for each individual trait.

# Define a function to create boxplots for each trait
create_boxplot <- function(ZosteropsMorph_species, trait) {
  ggplot(ZosteropsMorph_species, aes_string(x = "species", y = trait)) + 
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + # Boxplot without outliers
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, aes(color = species), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + # Add jitter for individual points
    labs(title = paste("Boxplot of", trait, "by Species"), x = "Species", y = trait) + 
    scale_color_manual(values = species_colors) +
    theme_minimal() # Minimal theme for better aesthetics
}
# List of traits to plot
traits <- c("BillCulmen", "BillNareTip", "BillDepth", "BillWidth", "Tarsus", "Wing", "Tail")
# Loop through each trait and create boxplots
for (trait in traits) {
  print(create_boxplot(ZosteropsMorph_species, trait)) # Print each boxplot
}

Pairwise t-tests by species.

# Conduct pairwise statistical tests between every pair of species for specified variables
results_list_species <- list() # Initialize a list to store results
# Loop through each trait for pairwise tests
for (trait in traits) {
  # Perform pairwise t-tests
  pairwise_results_species <- pairwise.t.test(ZosteropsMorph_species[[trait]], 
                                       ZosteropsMorph_species$species, 
                                       p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
  
  # Convert results to a tidy format
  tidy_results_species <- tidy(pairwise_results_species) %>%
    mutate(p.value = format.pval(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")) # Format p-values in scientific notation
  
  results_list_species[[trait]] <- tidy_results_species # Store results in the list
}
# Combine all results into a single data frame
final_results_species <- bind_rows(results_list_species, .id = "trait")
# Save the results to a CSV file
write.csv(final_results_species, "pairwise_test_results_species.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Select relevant variables and group by taxonomic group separating montanus into NORTH and SOUTH groups and japonicus into CONTINENTAL and OCEANIC groups and create datasets with the original data and log transformed data. 
ZosteropsMorph_groups <- ZosteropsMorph %>%
  select(Group, BillCulmen, BillNareTip, BillDepth, BillWidth, Tarsus, Wing, Tail) %>%
  group_by(Group)

ZosteropsMorph_LOG_groups <- ZosteropsMorph %>%
  select(Group, Log_BillCulmen, Log_BillNareTip, Log_BillDepth, Log_BillWidth, Log_Tarsus, Log_Wing, Log_Tail) %>%
  group_by(Group)

# Function to perform Kolmogorov-Smirnov test for each variable within each group
perform_ks_test <- function(group_data, variable) {
  # Create a list to store results
  results <- list()
  
  # Get unique groups
  unique_groups <- unique(group_data$Group)
  
  # Iterate over each unique group
  for (i in 1:length(unique_groups)) {
    # Filter data for the specific group
    group_name <- unique_groups[i]
    group_values <- group_data %>% filter(Group == group_name) %>% pull(variable)
    
    # Perform KS test with the first group's data as reference
    if (i == 1) {
      reference_values <- group_values
    } else {
      ks_test_result <- ks.test(group_values, reference_values)
      results[[group_name]] <- ks_test_result
    }
  }
  return(results)
}
# List of variables to test
variables <- c("Log_BillCulmen", "Log_BillNareTip", "Log_BillDepth", "Log_BillWidth", "Log_Tarsus", "Log_Wing", "Log_Tail")
# Perform KS tests for all variables
ks_results <- lapply(variables, function(var) perform_ks_test(ZosteropsMorph_LOG_groups, var))
# Naming the results list based on variables
names(ks_results) <- variables
# View results
ks_results

# Define a function to create boxplots for each trait
create_boxplot <- function(data, trait) {
  ggplot(data, aes_string(x = "Group", y = trait)) +
    geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA) + # Boxplot without outliers
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, aes(color = Group), size = 2, alpha = 0.5) + # Add jitter for individual points
    scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) + # Define colors for groups
    theme_minimal() + # Minimal theme for better aesthetics
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) # Adjust labels on X axis
}

# List of traits to plot
traits <- c("BillCulmen", "BillNareTip", "BillDepth", "BillWidth", "Tarsus", "Wing", "Tail")

# Loop through each trait and create boxplots
for (trait in traits) {
  assign(paste0("boxplot_groups_", trait), create_boxplot(ZosteropsMorph_groups, trait)) # Create and save boxplot as an object named by trait
}

# Conduct pairwise statistical tests between every pair of species for specified variables
results_list_groups <- list() # Initialize a list to store results
# Loop through each trait for pairwise tests
for (trait in traits) {
  # Perform pairwise t-tests
  pairwise_results_groups <- pairwise.t.test(ZosteropsMorph_groups[[trait]], 
                                       ZosteropsMorph_groups$Group, 
                                       p.adjust.method = "bonferroni")
  
  # Convert results to a tidy format
  tidy_results_groups <- tidy(pairwise_results_groups) %>%
    mutate(p.value = format.pval(p.value, digits = 2, format = "e")) # Format p-values in scientific notation
  
  results_list_groups[[trait]] <- tidy_results_groups # Store results in the list
}
# Combine all results into a single data frame
final_results_groups <- bind_rows(results_list_groups, .id = "trait")
# Save the results to a CSV file
write.csv(final_results_groups, "pairwise_test_results_groups.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Define the traits to create tables for
traits <- c('BillCulmen', 'BillNareTip', 'BillDepth', 'BillWidth', 'Tarsus', 'Wing', 'Tail')
# Loop through each trait to create and save tables
for (trait in traits) {
  # Filter data for the current trait
  trait_data_groups <- data %>% filter(trait == !!trait)
  
  # Create a readable table for the current trait
  table_name_groups <- paste0(trait, "_results_groups.csv")
  write_csv(trait_data_groups, table_name_groups)
}

Label settings for figures
Define common label settings across multiple figures.

grp_codes <- c("erythropleurus", "everetti", "japonicus", "japonicus_alani", "meyeni",
               "montanus_NORTH", "montanus_PALAWAN", "montanus_SOUTH",
               "nigrorum", "palpebrosus", "simplex")
pal <- setNames(ColorPal_CUSTOM, grp_codes)

# One-line labels (PCA legend): species italic, geography roman
lab_legend <- c(erythropleurus = "italic('Z. erythropleurus')", everetti = "italic('Z. everetti')",
                japonicus = "italic('Z. japonicus')", japonicus_alani = "italic('Z. japonicus alani')",
                meyeni = "italic('Z. meyeni')",
                montanus_NORTH = "italic('Z. montanus')~'N. Philippines'",
                montanus_PALAWAN = "italic('Z. montanus')~'Palawan'",
                montanus_SOUTH = "italic('Z. montanus')~'S. Philippines'",
                nigrorum = "italic('Z. nigrorum')", palpebrosus = "italic('Z. palpebrosus')",
                simplex = "italic('Z. simplex')")
# Two-line labels (DAPC bar headers)
lab_strip <- lab_legend
lab_strip[c("japonicus_alani", "montanus_NORTH", "montanus_PALAWAN", "montanus_SOUTH")] <-
  c("atop(italic('Z. japonicus'), italic('alani'))",
    "atop(italic('Z. montanus'), 'N. Philippines')",
    "atop(italic('Z. montanus'), 'Palawan')",
    "atop(italic('Z. montanus'), 'S. Philippines')")
